evidence: packages/telemetry — harness_telemetry.otel: frozen EventType stream → SpanSpec tree harness.run/plan/execution/review/change with DETERMINISTIC trace/span ids derived from runId (md5), so traces are reproducible and testable without an SDK
export_records replays spans through the REAL OTel SDK (TracerProvider + SimpleSpanProcessor, explicit OK/ERROR status) to any exporter

tests/test_otel.py: InMemorySpanExporter asserts the span tree (8 roots / 8 plans / 7 executions / 6 review verdicts / 3 change spans = 32); a REAL local HTTP collector receives the OTLP/HTTP protobuf POSTs and the wire body contains harness spans
W3C traceparent both directions: traceparent_for_run emits the header; parse_traceparent enforces strict version/id validation (rejects all-zero and ff-version); round-trip asserted
goldens: interop/golden/spans/run-{a1..b2}.json (8 runs) + traceparents.json
features.limits: Push-only export; endpoint/TLS/auth are collector-side deployment concerns, no live production collector exercised here. Span set covers the frozen vocabulary only.

evidence: metrics.quality_metrics + GET /api/v1/telemetry/quality + dashboard Quality tab; every figure carries its DEFINITIONS text verbatim

fixture corpus deliberately includes failure (run-a2 engine_failed), rework (run-a2 two attempts + review_failed; run-a3/run-b2 review_failed), abandonment (run-a4), blocked (run-a5), in-flight (run-a6)
exact denominators asserted in tests/test_metrics.py: tasks 8, started 7, accepted 3, rejected 2, rework 3, reworkRate 3/7, abandonmentRate 1/8
dashboard auth semantics tested: member pinned to own team, ?team=other → 403 TEAM_FORBIDDEN, admin org-wide, unwired principal dep → 503 AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED
goldens: quality_org.json, quality_team_b.json, member_scoped_quality.json, member_cross_team_forbidden.json, unauthenticated.json
features.limits: Quality is event-derived acceptance/rework/blocked/abandonment; review issue text is displayed but not semantically scored. UI is a minimal HTML page, not a product-grade frontend.

evidence: metrics.productivity_metrics + GET /api/v1/telemetry/productivity + dashboard tab: TTFUC percentiles, approval latency, approval→execution latency, sample counts per metric
fixtures: TTFUC values [35, 75, 85] min over 3 accepted runs → p50 75 / p90 85 (nearest-rank, documented); approval latency p50 2 / p90 30 including a slow-approval run (run-b1)
golden: productivity_org.json; sample counts published so thin data is visible (S4 acceptance: transparent denominators)
features.limits: Measures the harness timeline (plan/approve/execute/review/PR) only; human context work outside runs is invisible. Deliberately NO per-developer score — metrics are per-run/team.

evidence: metrics.cost_metrics over cost-ledger rows (Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, 4dp): costPerTask 3.0875 (24.70/8), costPerClaimedCompletion 4.2750 (17.10/4), costPerAcceptedChange 4.3667 (13.10/3) — claimed and accepted denominators are distinct published numbers
run-a3 regression guard: engine claimed completion, review rejected → its $4.00 counts in claimed, NOT accepted denominators
GET /api/v1/telemetry/cost + dashboard tab render all three with definitions
goldens: cost_org.json; asserted in tests/test_metrics.py::test_cost_per_task_claimed_and_accepted_are_distinct_numbers
features.limits: Depends on provider cost-ledger completeness (missing rows understate cost, never overstate). Infra/storage/human-review costs are out of scope.

evidence: TTFUC := pr_opened.ts − plan_proposed.ts for ACCEPTED runs only — anchored to the measured accepted change (PR + independent review pass), never to done_signal_received or the engine_completed claim
exposed as productivity endpoint {p50, p90, values} + harness.time_to_first_useful_change_minutes attribute on each harness.run span (OTel parity)
fixture proof: blocked/abandoned/rejected/active runs are excluded from the sample (3 accepted of 8 tasks); nearest-rank percentile documented in metrics.py
features.limits: Same clock source assumed for plan/pr timestamps (all events carry ts from one store); cross-service clock skew not normalized.

evidence: archive.Archive — SQLite runs+events built from the frozen stream; idempotent upsert ingest (re-ingest keeps 8 runs / 42 events), search by q/team/outcome/from/to with limit/offset and total count
PII/token scrubbing at INGEST: tests query the raw DB and prove neither goal text nor event payloads ever contain alice@example.com or ghp_/xoxb- tokens — scrubbed copies only
ownership fail-closed: visible_teams=None is admin org-wide, a set is team-scoped, empty set sees nothing; unattributed projects are org-visible only; dashboard member cross-team → 403
retention is an explicit per-ingest stamp (retentionUntil, default 90 days) + purge_expired removes runs and cascades to their events (tested: 8 runs + 0 orphan events)
goldens: archive_search_org.json, archive_search_login_team_b.json (goal shows [EMAIL]/[REDACTED]), run_detail_run-a1.json, run_detail_run-b2_scrubbed.json
features.limits: Single-node SQLite; q is a LIKE scan (pilot scale, not a search cluster). No archive UI beyond the table view; export API not included.

risks.risk: Malicious MCP servers, skills, plugins, or dependencies enter through the agent supply chain
controls: S1–S3 controls carried (digest-verified catalog, schema guards, capability tokens, connector signature schemes)
S4 adds openai/otel dependency surface: lower-bound pins only (opentelemetry-sdk>=1.25, -exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.25) — no lock file yet
telemetry ingest scrubs secrets before persistence (raw-DB proof in tests), archive auth fails closed, team scoping enforced at API layer
risks.remaining: Dependency locking/scanning for the telemetry stack and collector deployment hardening ship with Section 10 assembly.

risks.risk: Product cannot produce sufficient security evidence for procurement review
controls: S1–S3 evidence carried (OpenAPI snapshots, 57 goldens, 133 tests, real-gate smoke log, 4-wheel distribution verify)

S4: trace propagation with deterministic ids + real OTLP collector proof (interop with existing observability stacks), 21 new S4 goldens, 164 total tests, 5-wheel distribution verify with fresh-venv telemetry smoke
S4 archive: explicit retention policy, scrubbed-at-ingest persistence, 403/503 fail-closed access semantics — the kind of artifact procurement asks for
risks.remaining: No SOC2-style audit trail, external attestation, or pen-test; telemetry dashboards are pilot-grade.

risks.risk: Buyers cannot see measurable ROI beyond agent feels useful
controls: S4 ships the measurable accepted-change workflow end-to-end: accepted = pr_opened AND independent review pass; claimed completions tracked separately (run-a3 guard), transparent denominators for quality/rework/abandonment/TTFUC/cost, and pilot measurement instruments (docs/agent-program/a5/session-4/pilot-measurement.md) with opt-in/privacy checklist
metrics are computed from the already-frozen event stream — no invented telemetry, no ROI claims without a pilot
risks.remaining: No pilot has run: no real ROI/productivity numbers exist yet. S5 must deploy the instruments and report measured results with honest sample sizes.

risks.risk: Documentation/support too thin for independent adoption
controls: S3 controls carried (per-session reports, connector READMEs)
S4 adds packages/telemetry/README.md — usage, auth wiring, privacy/retention semantics, explicit known limits; pilot-measurement.md doubles as the operator-facing measurement contract
risks.remaining: No end-user support/onboarding flow or troubleshooting playbook beyond package READMEs.

risks.risk: Larger platforms bundle similar governance into existing paid tools
risks.remaining: Market risk; addressed by positioning evidence, not code.
